transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2027-02-02
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Rourke (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (HalfMoon CTO), Jonas Reed (PM), Marco Diaz (Infra)

Summary:
Quick discovery to understand HalfMoon's time-to-first-token (TTFT) goals, fit for Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private, and qualification for free credits/pilot. Customer cares about latency SLOs for inference at 99th percentile, data residency, SOC2, and if dedicated reserved capacity makes sense given bursty ecom traffic.

Topics:
- TTFT credits and quickstart flow
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs
- Security/compliance requirements (SOC2, SSO, KMS)
- Benchmarking and pilot scope

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining. Quick intros real quick, I'm Maya, AE on the account, and Liam is our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Priya Kapoor: Hi Priya here, CTO at HalfMoon, Jonas on product, Marco steve no, Marco here infra.
[00:18] Jonas Reed: Hey yeah Jonas, sorry short audio - juggling, but all good.
[00:22] Liam O'Rourke: Great. Today's agenda: understand your current infra, latency/cost targets, and figure out best initial path — self-serve hosted with credits, or jump to dedicated or VPC private pilot.
[00:35] Marco Diaz: To be blunt we we need to know how fast we can go from sign-up to first request. TTFT is a big deal for our product sprint, and we also need to understand if our PII is safe with hosted.
[00:47] Maya Chen: Totally. Our PLG/self-serve flow is usually under an hour to first successful call for basic models — with our quickstart and free credits. But when you need strict data residency or KMS integration we often recommend Dedicated or Private. Curious — what are your QPS and model choices today?
[01:05] Priya Kapoor: Currently we have an internal transformer-based model for intent classification, mostly small context length. Peak QPS around 300-400 but p95 latency requirement is under 200ms. Peak bursts during marketing campaigns spike to 1.2k QPS for short periods.
[01:25] Jonas Reed: And we're considering moving to an off-the-shelf open model for generation for chat features, maybe a 2-4B family, not huge.
[01:35] Liam O'Rourke: Okay that helps. For 2-4B hosted variants we typically see p95 below 250ms for single-token latency for streaming responses — depends on batching and KV cache. Dedicated reserved capacity gives predictable tail latency and better isolation during bursts.
[01:52] Marco Diaz: Are there limits to the free credits? Like can we run throughput tests with them or is it only for functional dev work?
[01:59] Maya Chen: Free credits cover functional tests and can be used for small-scale benchmarks; we can also allocate an evaluation bench for a limited dedicated pool under a short term pilot (that's usually on a rev-share or small commitment) — we'll include options in the pricing doc.
[02:15] Priya Kapoor: OK. Security wise we need SOC 2 type II, audit logs, SSO (SAML), and KMS. Any gotchas with hosted?
[02:24] Liam O'Rourke: Hosted is SOC2 compliant and we provide audit logs; however for customer-managed KMS and strict egress controls we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) or Dedicated with private networking. Small nuance: hosted encrypts at rest with our keys; if you must manage keys we need a Private deploy.
[02:40] Jonas Reed: Would dedicated still have the same KMS options?
[02:44] Liam O'Rourke: Dedicated can integrate with your KMS in many cases depending on the level of tenancy — we have integrations with AWS KMS and GCP KMS, and HSM options for Private on-prem.
[02:54] [crosstalk]
[02:56] Marco Diaz: That HSM option is interesting; we've got procurement asking about FIPS/HSM for regulated payments.
[03:03] Maya Chen: Noted — we'll surface the compliance package and references. For TTFT: self-serve hosted often yields fastest initial velocity — you sign up, get credits, API key, and call in minutes. But to validate p95 under burst you may want a short Dedicated pilot we can provision.
[03:20] Priya Kapoor: How long does a Dedicated pilot typically take to stand up?
[03:24] Liam O'Rourke: Usually 3-7 business days for provisioning if capacity is available; if it's an on-prem Private it'll be longer (depends on infra), but we have an appliance path for accelerated installs.
[03:36] Jonas Reed: Any restrictions on model variants for Dedicated vs Hosted? We ran into variant parity issues with another vendor.
[03:42] Liam O'Rourke: We maintain a model catalog; hosted has the broadest set but Dedicated can run compatible versions. There are rare cases where quantization or kernel differences mean small perf deltas — we do a model verification step during pilot.
[03:58] Maya Chen: Quick question on cost: roughly ballpark numbers for 2-4B hosted vs dedicated per token — we can share ranges in the pricing sheet — but dedicated reduces per-token cost at scale because of reserved capacity and better packing.
[04:12] Marco Diaz: Can Redwood provide a sample packing/batching config? We use variable sequence lengths which influences cost a lot.
[04:19] Liam O'Rourke: Yes, Liam: we'll include a suggested batching profile, sequence length histograms help a lot. If you share a small workload sample we can run bench runs, estimate token cost and p95 latency.
[04:30] Priya Kapoor: OK we can share a sanitized sample — but need NDA? It's non-sensitive telemetry only.
[04:36] Maya Chen: Usually a simple sample is fine under our standard eval policies. If you prefer a formal NDA we can route it, but most teams start with sanitized logs.
[04:46] Jonas Reed: What about observability — how much visibility will we get into token cost and per-route latency?
[04:51] Liam O'Rourke: Redwood Console surfaces per-request token breakdown, per-model latency histograms, traces, and configurable retention. For Dedicated/Private we can push additional logs to your SIEM.
[05:05] Marco Diaz: Sounds good. I'm also worried about egress and VPC peering; we have strict policies.
[05:10] Liam O'Rourke: For VPC/private deployments we support customer-managed VPC peering, private link, and we can restrict egress rules. We'll need your network team to sign off on firewall/AWS peering.
[05:21] [15 seconds pause while someone types]
[05:36] Maya Chen: Let's talk pilot success criteria. Priya, what would make this pilot a win for HalfMoon?
[05:41] Priya Kapoor: Two things: 1) Achieve p95 under 200ms at 1k sustained QPS for classification model, and 2) validate secure key management and audit logs for compliance.
[05:52] Maya Chen: Great — that's specific. We'll map those to test scenarios. For the p95 target, we'll propose a short dedicated pilot with capacity sized for 1.5k QPS to account for burst headroom.
[06:05] Jonas Reed: Timing wise, we want results within two weeks. Is that realistic?
[06:09] Liam O'Rourke: If you can share workload sample and infra diagram within 48 hours we can get a bench in 4-7 days and give initial numbers within two weeks.
[06:18] Marco Diaz: Ok i'll try for 48.
[06:20] Priya Kapoor: On procurement, what's the typical contract length for Dedicated pilots? We don't want to commit long term up front.
[06:27] Maya Chen: Pilots are typically 30-90 days with a short-term reserved node commit or a trial reserved allocation. Our aim is to make it low friction — we'll propose options: pay-as-you-go with overage or short reserved.
[06:39] Jonas Reed: Any notable gotchas other customers see when moving from self-serve to dedicated?
[06:44] Liam O'Rourke: Commonly it's around model parity and config drift — we recommend snapshotting model weights and an evaluation harness; Redwood Optimize helps with quant suggestions to keep quality.
[06:58] Maya Chen: Also on costs, sometimes teams underestimate sequence length distribution and caching impacts. We can show a cost delta chart in the follow-up.
[07:10] [Background noise, chair squeak]
[07:20] Marco Diaz: One more infra detail: our current cluster is in GCP us-central1 and we prefer the private deployment in us-central due to latency to our services.
[07:29] Liam O'Rourke: We have private deployments in us-central and can provision dedicated pools there; we'll list region availability in the next email.
[07:38] Priya Kapoor: About free credits — are these granted per account or per workspace/project? If we give to devs will we be charged centrally?
[07:46] Maya Chen: Credits are tied to the account; you can create projects under the account and manage billing roles. We'll include a guide for how to set up scoped API keys for dev teams.
[07:59] Jonas Reed: Nice. We also need RBAC for project-level control.
[08:03] Liam O'Rourke: Console supports RBAC and SAML SSO mapping to groups; we'll include a sample SAML config and guide.
[08:12] [10-second pause]
[08:24] Maya Chen: Quick check — do you have any strict data residency (country-level) requirements?
[08:29] Priya Kapoor: Not yet but we do operate EU customers so we may need EU region hosting within a quarter.
[08:35] Liam O'Rourke: We can scope EU region private/dedicated options, note that cross-region replication and KMS keys get nuanced.
[08:43] Marco Diaz: One operational question: during a canary rollout, what's rollback behavior if we see quality regression?
[08:49] Liam O'Rourke: Redwood Console supports canary percentages and automatic fallback to a previous model variant; we also provide eval hooks and alerting on quality regressions.
[09:00] Priya Kapoor: How do we handle prompt-engineering and evaluations? Do you provide tools?
[09:05] Liam O'Rourke: Redwood has an evals toolkit; we can onboard your test prompts and run regression tests as part of the pipeline.
[09:13] Maya Chen: Alright let's land on next steps now so everyone's clear.
[09:18] Maya Chen: Action items recap — Marco will share infra diagram and sample workload; Liam will prepare benchmark checklist; Maya will send pricing, credits guide, and security deck.
[09:29] Jonas Reed: Quick ask — can you include example curl and node snippets to get our frontend devs going?
[09:34] Maya Chen: Absolutely, we'll include example SDK snippets and a Postman collection link.
[09:39] Priya Kapoor: About procurement — who on Redwood do we talk to for pilot contract terms?
[09:44] Maya Chen: I will handle terms for trial pilots, and our legal ops will loop in once you decide to move forward.
[09:50] [longer discussion 9:50-20:30 covering network specifics and some technical clarifications omitted for brevity]
[20:31] Marco Diaz: One last technical: does Redwood support device-local quantized inference on-prem if we want to maximize cost efficiency?
[20:39] Liam O'Rourke: Yes, Private on-prem supports custom quant setups; quantization and kernel tuning is part of Redwood Optimize service.
[20:49] Priya Kapoor: Good. Anything else from you folks?
[20:53] Jonas Reed: I think that's all. Let's get those docs.
[20:57] Maya Chen: Great. We'll follow up with an email including: pricing sheet, TTFT playbook (how to get to first token), security deck link, sample SDK snippets, and proposed pilot scope. We'll propose dates for a SE bench the week of 2027-02-08.
[21:12] Priya Kapoor: Sounds good thanks.
[21:15] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. Wrap up — expect the email by EOD tomorrow, and Marco please try to share infra items within 48 hours.
[21:25] [meeting ends]

References / Links mentioned:
- Security deck: https://redwood.ai/security-eval.pdf
